title: More than 200 protesters still in police custody after stalled inquest
summary: An inquest delay has left arrested ASEAN protesters in custody.

blocks.text: November 17, 2026 | 3:42pm

Protesters clash with police officers during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on November 15, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta. Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — Hundreds of protesters arrested during an anti-Pax Silica demonstration in Muntinlupa City remained in police custody on Tuesday, November 17, after inquest proceedings failed to proceed the previous day, prolonging their detention without formal charges filed in court.
The protesters were arrested Sunday, November 15, during a demonstration opposing the US-led Pax Silica initiative and the visit of President Donald Trump for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

They were taken to Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City, where they remained as of Tuesday. Protest organizers estimated that nearly 300 people were arrested, while police reported more than 200 are still in custody.

Jesus Monasterial, deputy secretary-general of the Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magbubukid sa Timog Katagalugan, told ABS-CBN's "TV Patrol" that Monday's inquest proceedings fell through because the prosecutor failed to arrive.
Inquest are when a prosecutor determines whether a person arrested without a warrant should face criminal charges.
Monasterial said the delay left protesters in custody for more than 30 hours without formal charges filed against them.

He also said authorities had asked some detainees to sign waivers under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code, which sets time limits for delivering people arrested without warrants to the proper judicial authorities.
Under Article 125, the limits are 12 hours for offenses punishable by light penalties, 18 hours for correctional penalties and 36 hours for afflictive or capital penalties.
A waiver may allow a detainee to remain in custody beyond the applicable period while seeking a preliminary investigation, but it must be voluntary and executed with the assistance of counsel.
The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO), meanwhile, denied allegations that it had deprived those in its custody of legal assistance, food and other basic necessities.
UP students, campus journalists detained
At least 50 students from the University of the Philippines system were among those arrested during the Muntinlupa protest, according to reports from university units and student publications.
UP Diliman called for the immediate release of 10 of its students on Monday, November 16. Among them was a staff member of the Philippine Collegian, the university's official student publication.
The Collegian reported that a preliminary bail amount of P30,000 had been set for the staff member's release.
At UP Los Baños (UPLB), various colleges confirmed that 44 students were in detention.
The detainees included 10 staff members of UPLB Perspective, the campus' official student publication.

UPLB's Standing Committee on National Issues and the Promotion and Protection of Academic Freedom and Human Rights said police had informed detainees that they would face complaints for illegal assembly and public disturbance after allegedly refusing orders to stop their protest.
The specific offenses to be pursued and whether criminal cases have been filed in court remain unconfirmed.
DFA declines comment. Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro declined to comment Monday on the arrests during the ASEAN Summit.
At a press conference Monday, she said the discussions among regional leaders had focused on regional matters rather than domestic issues.
The summit has drawn protests against several initiatives, including the US-led Pax Silica framework, which aims to secure semiconductor and artificial intelligence supply chains.
